findings.summary: os.Chmod runs on filepath.Dir(dst) unconditionally, even without a perm argument, so it can change the mode of the working directory or a shared existing directory and may fail with EPERM on directories the process doesn't own.
The perm argument is applied to the directory rather than the file, undocumented, so a caller passing 0o644 gets a directory without an execute bit and writing the file fails with permission denied.

TestSaveUploadedFileWithPermission uses filepath.Dir("permission_test") which is ".", so it chmods the package directory and leaves a stray file instead of using t.TempDir(); the failure test depends on test/ being uncreatable and can leave a test directory behind.
